diagram_math_checks.details: The figure represents O = S_R^2 intersect {x1,x2,x3 >= 0}, exactly step 7.1. The linear projection of normalized coordinates sends e1 to (2.5,-0.7), e2 to (-2,-1.1), e3 to (0,2.5); labels restore scale R. Thus the three labelled vertices represent Re1, Re2, Re3.

The three plotted curves are respectively projections of cos(t)e1+sin(t)e2, cos(t)e2+sin(t)e3, and cos(t)e3+sin(t)e1 for 0 <= t <= pi/2. Each has unit norm, nonnegative coordinates and one zero coordinate, so it is exactly the corresponding quarter great circle from step 7.1, geodesic by F4. Endpoints match consecutively; independent draw commands show all three sides and their closure. Each vertex has degree two. No arrows assert orientation.

At Rei, the two inward tangent directions are ej and ek for distinct i,j,k, hence their ambient dot product is zero. F5 and step 7.1 identify this with the intrinsic metric, justifying each pi/2 label. Caption explicitly says that projected planar angles are not the intrinsic angles.

Step 7.1 integrates R^2 sin(theta) on [0,pi/2]^2 to pi R^2/2. Three pi/2 angles sum to 3pi/2, agreeing with pi+A/R^2 from step 6.1. Both labels restate proved values; rigorous Verification is unchanged and independent of the illustration.
